quick.definition: able to move fast; also ready to think or respond.
examples: Take a quick look at this.

quixotic.definition: unrealistic and overly idealistic, often in a way that ignores practical limits
examples: His quixotic plan failed in the real world.
She tried a quixotic rescue attempt.

quell.definition: to put an end to something, especially strong feelings or violence
examples: The police moved to quell the unrest.
She tried to quell her anger.

quatrain.definition: a stanza with four lines in poetry
examples: The poem uses quatrains to organize the story.
Each quatrain rhymes in the same pattern.

quote.definition: the exact words of someone, written or spoken; also, a short section from a text
examples: Please add a quote from the book.
The quote at the end summarizes the theme.

quote.definition: to repeat exact words from a source or a person
examples: She quoted the letter to support her claim.
You should quote the author correctly.

quote.definition: to give a price for a service or product
examples: They quoted $300 for the repairs.
Can you quote the cost of the trip?

quaternion.definition: a mathematical object used in advanced algebra and 3D rotations
examples: A quaternion is used to represent orientation in 3D graphics.
The program uses quaternions to rotate objects.

quiver.definition: to shake slightly or move up and down with small fast movements
examples: The candle flame quivered in the draft.
Her lip quivered when she tried not to cry.

quibble.definition: a small objection or argument over wording that avoids the main issue
examples: He kept making quibbles instead of answering the question.
Don’t waste time on quibbles.

quibble.definition: to argue about small details or wording rather than the main point
examples: She quibbled over the wording of the contract.
They quibbled instead of discussing the real problem.

quarrel.definition: an argument between people, usually short but unpleasant.
examples: They had a quarrel about money.
A quarrel broke out in the hallway.

quarrel.definition: to argue with someone, often repeatedly.
examples: They quarrelled over small things.
Stop quarrelling and listen.

questioning.definition: the act of asking questions to get information.
examples: Questioning began immediately after the incident.
She answered calmly during the questioning.

questioning.definition: relating to asking questions or demanding answers.
examples: His questioning look made her nervous.
The questioning tone sounded strict.

quiet.definition: making little or no sound; not loud
examples: The library is quiet after five o’clock.
Please keep your voice quiet in the hospital.

quiet.definition: not showing feelings or acting in an emotionally calm way
examples: She stayed quiet during the argument.
His quiet smile reassured everyone.

quiet.definition: to make less noise or to become calm and silent
examples: They turned off the music to quiet the room.
The storm finally quieted in the evening.

quietude.definition: a state of being quiet and peaceful
examples: She enjoyed the quietude of the morning.
The room filled with quietude after the speeches ended.

quirnel.definition: no standard modern english word or common usage found for this form. did you mean quirel, quern, or another spelling?
examples: If you share the correct spelling, I will generate an accurate dictionary entry.

quarry.definition: a place where stone or other materials are taken from the ground for building or industry
examples: The quarry provided limestone for the construction.
Cars passed the quarry every morning.

quarry.definition: to search for something, often resources, by digging or seeking
examples: They quarry the region for valuable stone.
The team quarries new ideas in meetings.

quoin.definition: a wedge-shaped stone or block at the corner of a building, often used for structural support or decoration
examples: The house has decorative quoins at each corner.
Workers repaired a damaged quoin.

query.definition: a question or request for information
examples: Send your query to the support team.
I have a query about my billing.

query.definition: to ask about something or request information
examples: They queried the results before accepting them.
The client queried the charge on the invoice.

qualm.definition: a feeling of doubt or worry about whether something is right
examples: She had no qualm about speaking up.
I felt a qualm when I realized the plan was risky.

quagmire.definition: a difficult situation that is hard to escape
examples: The project became a quagmire after delays.
Negotiations turned into a quagmire.

quire.definition: a group of singers, usually in church or formal settings
examples: The quire sang hymns at the service.
We listened to the quire perform in the cathedral.

quag.definition: soft, muddy ground that sinks under weight
examples: The path turned to quag and became dangerous.
His boot sank into the quag.

quarto.definition: a size of book or page format made by folding a sheet twice
examples: The book was printed in quarto size.
A quarto edition was released in the 1800s.
